task_prompts.click-ac655f8a:
HelpFormatter.write_text() doesn't use the full available width when wrapping text, leaving the wrapped lines noticeably shorter than the formatter's width would allow. For example:

```python
import click
text = "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit"
formatter = click.HelpFormatter(width=len("  Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet,"))
formatter.current_indent = 2
formatter.write_text(text)
print(formatter.getvalue())
```

I'd expect the output to wrap using as much of the line width as possible (e.g. "  Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet,\n  consectetur adipiscing elit\n"), but the wrapping is off. Please fix write_text() so it correctly uses the full line width.
task_prompts.click-166b3126: The show_default behavior on Option doesn't correctly account for precedence between the option-level show_default and the context-level show_default. Depending on the combination of ctx.show_default and Option(show_default=...), the wrong decision is made about whether to print "default: ..." in the help text. For example, setting show_default=True at the Context level should be overridden by an explicit show_default=False on the Option, and vice versa, but currently this isn't handled consistently. Please fix Option.get_help_record() (or wherever the precedence is resolved) so that an explicit per-option show_default always takes priority over the context-level setting, falling back to the context value only when the option doesn't specify one.
task_prompts.click-d251cb0a:
When a custom ParamType subclass doesn't explicitly set a `name` attribute, calling `to_info_dict()` on an instance fails or returns an incorrect/missing name instead of falling back to something sensible like the class name. For example:

```python
import click

class TestType(click.ParamType):
    pass

print(TestType().to_info_dict()["name"])
```

I'd expect this to return "TestType" (derived from the class), but it doesn't. Please fix ParamType.to_info_dict() to handle types that don't define a name.
task_prompts.click-1b524bb3:
When a required option with an envvar is missing and show_envvar=True is set, the "Missing option" error message doesn't mention the environment variable name, even though it's supposed to help users understand where the value could come from. For example:

```python
import click

cli = click.Command("cli", params=[click.Option(["--foo"], envvar="bar", show_envvar=True, required=True)])
cli.main([], standalone_mode=False)
```

Running this without setting the `bar` env var should produce an error like `Error: Missing option '--foo' (env var: 'bar').`, but the env var hint is missing from the message. Please fix the missing-parameter error message to include the env var name when show_envvar is enabled.
task_prompts.click-0cd28d65: When a group uses custom `help_option_names` (e.g. `-h` and `--help`) and a subcommand defines its own option that reuses one of those names, the 'Try ... for help' hint shown on usage errors can point to a help flag name that is actually shadowed and unusable on that subcommand. For example, if a subcommand has `click.option("--help-file", "--help")`, running it with a missing required argument should suggest `-h` (the still-available help name), not `--help`. If every configured help name is shadowed, no hint should be shown at all. Please fix the error hint so it only ever references a help option name that is actually available on that command, preferring the longest available name.
task_prompts.click-2468b709:
On non-Windows platforms, `click.prompt()` and `click.confirm()` print the prompt text separately from calling the input function, which breaks readline features like backspace and line-wrapping while typing at the prompt. Additionally, when `err=True` and/or `prompt_suffix=""` is used, output ends up split incorrectly between stdout and stderr. For example:

```python
click.prompt("Prompt to stderr with no suffix", prompt_suffix="", err=True)
```

should write the full prompt text `"Prompt to stderr with no suffix"` cleanly to stderr with nothing leaking to stdout, but currently part of the text is misplaced. The full prompt (including any suffix) should be passed directly to the underlying input function so terminal line-editing behaves correctly. Please fix this.
task_prompts.click-19fd4d6e:
Fish shell completion breaks when an option's help text contains literal newlines (e.g. using a `\b` preformatted block). For example:

```python
Option(
    ["--at", "--attachment-type"],
    type=(str, str),
    multiple=True,
    help="\b\nAttachment with explicit mimetype,\n--at image.jpg image/jpeg",
)
```

When generating fish completions for a command using this option, the multiline help text isn't escaped, resulting in malformed completion output (extra/garbled lines) instead of a single completion entry with the newlines escaped as `\n`. Please fix the fish completion output so multiline help strings are handled correctly.
task_prompts.click-c943271a:
When using click.prompt(..., hide_input=True) together with a custom ParamType whose convert() calls self.fail() with a message built from the typed value, the error message shown to the user doesn't behave correctly with input hiding. For example:
```python
import click

class Password(click.ParamType):
    name = "password"
    def convert(self, value, param, ctx):
        if len(value) < 10:
            self.fail(f"{value} is too short", param, ctx)
        return value

click.prompt("Password", type=Password(), hide_input=True)
```
With hide_input=True, click should still surface the custom validation message, but any occurrence of the raw typed value inside that message (whether it appears quoted via repr or bare) must be masked out (e.g. replaced with '***') rather than leaked in plain text or dropped entirely, including cases where the value appears multiple times or mixed with a static message that never references it. Please fix this.
task_prompts.click-3bb230dc:
HelpFormatter.write_usage produces a broken usage line when there are no args to show. For example:
```python
import click
f = click.HelpFormatter()
f.write_usage("myprog", "")
print(repr(f.getvalue()))
```
This currently prints just a blank line instead of "Usage: myprog\n". The same problem shows up end-to-end: a Command created with `options_metavar=""` and no parameters renders a blank/garbled usage line in its --help output instead of "Usage: cli". A custom or styled prefix passed to write_usage should also still be honored correctly even when args is empty. Please fix this so the usage line renders correctly regardless of whether args is empty.
task_prompts.click-c3535905: Shell completion for fish is broken (a recent change regressed it) and multi-line option help also causes bad output. Reproduce by invoking a CLI with a command that has options with help text under fish completion, e.g. setting `_CLI_COMPLETE=fish_complete` with `COMP_WORDS`/`COMP_CWORD` env vars for a CLI that has an option whose help string contains multiple lines (using the `\b` no-rewrap marker). The completion output is emitted in the wrong format for fish (newline-separated blocks instead of fish's expected `type,value` / `type,value\thelp` lines), and when an option's help text spans multiple lines it either breaks completion or leaks literal newlines into the output instead of escaping them. Please fix fish completion so it produces correctly formatted, single-line entries even when help text contains newlines.
task_prompts.click-fc5c7f45:
When an exception is raised while content is being displayed through click's pager (the code path used via `click.echo_via_pager` / `click.get_pager_file`), the original exception can get replaced by an unrelated error on Windows. Reproduce with:
```python
import click

with click.get_pager_file():
    raise RuntimeError("boom")
```
The RuntimeError should propagate normally. Instead, on the Windows temp-file pager backend, the temporary file is not closed before it is unlinked in the cleanup path when an exception occurs, so deleting it raises `PermissionError: [WinError 32] The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process`, which masks the real error the user was trying to see. Please fix this so the temp file is always closed before cleanup runs, even when an exception is raised.
